paper.title: Optimal cross-learning for contextual bandits with unknown context distributions

settings.name_in_paper: Contextual bandits with cross-learning, adversarial losses, i.i.d. contexts from unknown distribution
unmapped: cross-learning feedback: the learner observes the loss of the played arm for every context, not only the current one
context distribution nu is unknown to the learner; number of contexts may be arbitrary (bound independent of |C|)
regret against the best fixed mapping from contexts to arms
optionally context-dependent fixed sets of active arms A_c (non-uniform action sets), covered by the analysis
settings.definition_quote: At the start of the problem, an oblivious adversary selects a bounded loss function $\ell_{tk}:\calC\rightarrow[0,1]$ for every round $t \in [T]$ and every arm $k\in[K]$. In each round $t$, then we begin by sampling a context $c_t\sim\nu$ i.i.d.\ from an unknown distribution $\nu$ over $\calC$, and we reveal this context to the learner. ... Notably, the learner observes the loss for \textit{every} context $c \in \calC$, but only for the arm $A_t$ they actually played.

settings.name_in_paper: Learning to bid in first-price auctions with unknown value distribution
unmapped: first-price auction: context is private value v_t ~ nu i.i.d. (unknown) in [0,1], action is bid b_t in [0,1], highest competing bid m_t chosen obliviously by adversary
binary feedback: only whether the auction was won
regret against best fixed mapping from values to bids
settings.definition_quote: In auction $t$, they have a value $v_t \in [0, 1]$ for the current item being sold, with $v_t$ being drawn i.i.d. from some unknown distribution $\nu$ supported on $[0, 1]$. They submit a bid $b_t \in [0, 1]$ into the auction. We let $m_t \in [0, 1]$ denote the highest other bid ... (and allow the adversary to choose the sequence of $m_t$ obliviously in advance). ... the bidder only observes the binary feedback of whether or not they won the item

settings.name_in_paper: Sleeping bandits with stochastic action set
unmapped: available arm sets S_t drawn i.i.d. from an unknown, arbitrary (possibly correlated) distribution
regret against best fixed policy mapping available sets to arms
settings.definition_quote: Each round $t$ (for $T$ rounds), a non-empty subset $S_t \subseteq [K]$ of the arms is declared to be ``active''. The learner must select one of the active arms $k \in S_t$, upon which they receive some loss $\ell_{tk}$. We assume here that the losses are chosen by an oblivious adversary, but the $S_t$ are sampled independently every round from an unknown distribution $\nu$.

algorithms.name: Contextual cross-learning algorithm for the unknown distribution setting (Algorithm 1; epoch-based EXP3/FTRL with snapshots and rejection sampling)

bound.expression: (gamma_c + iota/L_ep + gamma_c**2*L_ep/iota + eta + exp(-iota)*T/L_ep)*K*T + log(K)/eta + L_ep

symbols.gamma_c: confidence parameter gamma of the algorithm

source.label: thm:main
source.quote: For any $\eta \leq \frac{\gamma}{2(2L\gamma+\iota)}$, $\gamma \geq \frac{16\iota}{L}$, $\iota \geq \log(8K/\gamma)$, \pref{alg: cross learning ftrl} satisfies \begin{align*} \Reg = O\left(\left(\gamma+\frac{\iota}{L}+\frac{\gamma^2 L}{\iota}+\eta+\exp(-\iota)\frac{T}{L}\right) KT + \frac{\log(K)}{\eta}+L\right)\,. \end{align*}

results.notes: Reg defined as max over policies of expectation (losses oblivious), hence pseudo_regret. Analysis covers non-uniform context-dependent action sets.

tuning: L = sqrt(iota K T / log K)

source.label: thm:main
source.quote: Tuning $\iota = 2\log(8KT)$, $L=\sqrt{\frac{\iota KT}{\log(K)}} = \widetilde\Theta(\sqrt{KT})$, $\gamma = \frac{16\iota}{L}$ ... and $\eta = \frac{\gamma}{2(2L\gamma+\iota)}$ ... yields a regret bound of $\Reg=\widetilde O\left(\sqrt{KT}\right)$

results.notes: Tuned consequence stated in text after Theorem 1. Õ hides logs in K and T, independent of number of contexts.

tuning: bids discretized to multiples of T^{-1/3} (K = T^{1/3})

source.quote: There exists an efficient learning algorithm that achieves a regret bound of $\widetilde{O}(T^{2/3})$ for the problem of learning to bid in a first-price auction with an unknown value distribution.

results.notes: Obtained by applying Algorithm 1 with K = T^{1/3} discretized bids. Regret type follows Theorem 1 (expectation).

source.quote: There exists an efficient learning algorithm that achieves a regret bound of $\widetilde O(\sqrt{KT})$ for the sleeping bandits problem with stochastic action sets drawn from an unknown distribution.

results.notes: O(K) time per round per paper.
